pattern_name: Hierarchical block input-delay budget from unimplemented launch block
situation: Two blocks A and B in same clock domain; B has input port driven by A; A not yet implemented; need set_input_delay on B's input so B's implementation leaves enough margin for A to be built later.
derivation: Assume clock period T = 10ns (confidence 0.2 — example only). Budget split: launch logic (A internal) = 0.50  T = 5ns (confidence 0.4 on 50% split), interconnect/wire delay = 0.10  T = 1ns (confidence 0.4 on 10% interconnect), capture internal (B input-to-flop) = 0.40  T = 4ns (confidence 0.4 on 40% capture). set_input_delay -clock clk [get_ports IN] value = launch + interconnect = 0.60  T = 6ns. Remaining time for B's internal logic = T - input_delay - T_setup = 4ns - T_setup. If A later requires more than 5ns, B's budget is already consumed and integration fails.
wrong_way: Setting input_delay = T (period) leaves 0ns for B internal logic — always fails STA. Setting input_delay = 0 leaves full period for B but A can never meet its launch delay in integration. Silently breaks: over-constrained B wastes area/power; under-constrained B passes STA but system fails at integration.
defense: Engineer presents the budget spreadsheet showing the 50/10/40 split justified by pipeline stage count and wire-load estimates from similar blocks; claims this is conservative for A's complexity.
signoff_risk: Too tight: B over-optimized, wasted power/area, possible failure to close timing. Too loose: A cannot meet launch delay at integration, system timing failure on silicon.
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: OCV/POCV requires extra 10-15% margin in budget split (confidence 0.6), reducing the capture-side allocation

pattern_name: False path vs multicycle on slow control/configuration registers
situation: Configuration or reset signal that changes only at boot or infrequently; crosses flops in same clock domain but data is not required to be valid next cycle.
derivation: If signal only needs to propagate in N cycles (e.g., N=2 for a two-cycle config write), set_multicycle_path N -from [src_regs] -to [dest_regs]. For same-clock slow control, set_multicycle_path 2. Hold check defaults to same edge; add set_multicycle_path 1 -hold to keep hold check at launch edge. Arithmetic: setup check moves to cycle N, so required time = N*T - T_setup. If truly async and never timed (e.g., test reset), set_false_path -from [src] -to [dest].
wrong_way: Setting set_false_path on a signal that actually changes at operational speed — silently breaks: chip works at low speed or in simulation but fails intermittently at target frequency because data arrives late relative to capture edge.
defense: Engineer shows waveform or protocol spec proving signal only toggles once per N cycles; points to RTL state machine guaranteeing N-cycle separation.
signoff_risk: Too tight (no exception): wasted effort fixing unneeded paths, area/power penalty. Too loose (false path when multicycle needed): data corruption if signal changes faster than assumed; intermittent system failure.

situation: Block synthesis or pre-CTS, before final clock tree and routing; want margin so later stages don't invalidate timing closure.
derivation: Target clock period = T. Set constraint to 0.80  T (i.e., 20% margin) (confidence 0.5 on 20% being typical; some teams use 10-15%). Alternatively, set_clock_uncertainty additional 0.05  T (confidence 0.5 on 5% extra). Arithmetic: if T=5ns, constrain to 4ns. Relax to T after CTS or route. Over-constraint removed in final signoff constraint set.
wrong_way: Over-constraining by 50% (0.5*T) — tool cannot close timing, wasted iterations, team blames flow. Or forgetting to relax before tapeout — chip ships over-margined, wasted power/area, no benefit.
defense: Engineer cites historical data from prior tapeouts showing post-CTS insertion delay consumed 15-20% of period (confidence 0.5); margin chosen to absorb this.
signoff_risk: Too tight: area/power penalty, possible failure to close timing, schedule slip. Too loose (no margin): post-P&R timing fails, late ECO required, tapeout delay.
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: over-constrain by less (e.g., 10%) because tool has harder time closing on aggressive targets due to wire delay dominance (confidence 0.55)

pattern_name: Virtual clock for external-device input timing
situation: Chip receives data from external device with known t_co, board trace delay; need to constrain input port relative to external clock.
derivation: Create virtual clock: create_clock -name vclk -period T. set_input_delay -clock vclk -max t_co_ext + t_board_delay [get_ports IN]. Assume T=10ns (confidence 0.2), t_co_ext=2ns (confidence 0.3), t_board=1ns (confidence 0.3). Input delay = 3ns. Required internal arrival = T - input_delay - T_setup = 10 - 3 - 0.1 = 6.9ns for internal logic.
wrong_way: Using real internal clock with offset instead of virtual clock — creates false clock relationship, breaks timing analysis. Ignoring board delay — silently breaks: STA passes but system fails at board level because trace delay was not accounted.
defense: Engineer presents external device datasheet t_co max, board stack-up trace delay estimate, and system-level timing budget showing the arithmetic.
signoff_risk: Too tight: STA fails unnecessarily, over-design of input buffer. Too loose: system integration failure, external device setup not met at board level.

pattern_name: Generated clock from divider for low-power domain
situation: Internal divided clock from PLL or RTL divider for a slower domain; need to constrain paths through divided clock and crossings back to fast domain.
derivation: create_generated_clock -name clk_div2 -source [master_pin] -divide_by 2 [divider_output]. Period of clk_div2 = 2*T. For paths from fast to slow domain: launch period = T, capture period = 2T. Default setup check at first slow-clock edge (T) may be too tight; often set_multicycle_path 2 -to [slow_domain_regs] to allow full 2T. Arithmetic: if T=5ns, fast-to-slow default setup check at 5ns; with multicycle 2, check at 10ns.
wrong_way: Using create_clock instead of create_generated_clock — breaks clock relationship, timing engine treats as async, no cross-domain paths analyzed. Silently breaks: paths between domains either falsely pass (no check) or are over-constrained.
defense: Engineer shows clock tree schematic, divider ratio, and cross-domain path report proving correct clock relationship and multicycle exception.
signoff_risk: Wrong command or missing multicycle: complete loss of valid timing checks or false violations; silicon failure if critical path escapes.

pattern_name: Asynchronous CDC handshake max-delay constraint for MTBF
situation: Two async clock domains with handshake; clocks unrelated; need to bound metastability probability with max-delay on synchronizer flops.
derivation: set_clock_groups -asynchronous -group {clkA} -group {clkB}. For synchronizer flops, set_max_delay 0.5 * T_fast (confidence 0.4 on 0.5 factor; typical range 0.3-0.7). If T_fast=2ns, max_delay=1ns. This bounds the time for signal to propagate through first sync flop, reducing metastability window. Arithmetic: MTBF ∝ exp(delay/metastability_time_constant); tighter max_delay improves MTBF.
wrong_way: No constraint at all — no MTBF check, potential for rare metastability failures in field. Silently breaks: chip passes STA but fails intermittently in system due to unresolved CDC.
defense: Engineer presents MTBF calculation spreadsheet showing max_delay value achieves target MTBF (e.g., >1 year mean time between failures) given process metastability parameters.
signoff_risk: Too tight: routing congestion, wasted resources on short paths. Too loose: metastability not bounded, system fails intermittently; field returns.
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: smaller nodes have smaller metastability window, so max_delay needs to be tighter (e.g., 0.3*T_fast, confidence 0.6); POCV also affects MTBF calculation

pattern_name: Clock uncertainty budgeting for PLL jitter and variation
situation: Setting clock_uncertainty for setup/hold to account for PLL jitter, AOCV/POCV, and clock-tree variation at various implementation stages.
derivation: Uncertainty = PLL_jitter + variation_margin. Assume PLL_jitter = 0.05  T (confidence 0.5 on 5%), AOCV_margin = 0.02  T (confidence 0.5 on 2%). Total = 0.07  T. For T=5ns, uncertainty = 0.35ns. Applied via set_clock_uncertainty 0.35 [get_clocks clk]. Pre-CTS: add estimated clock skew (e.g., 0.10T, confidence 0.4). Post-CTS: remove skew, keep jitter + variation.
wrong_way: Setting uncertainty = 0 — no margin for jitter; silicon fails at speed. Setting too high (e.g., 0.3*T) — cannot close timing, wasted area/power. Silently breaks: wrong uncertainty hides real timing problems or creates false failures.
defense: Engineer presents PLL datasheet jitter spec, process variation model (AOCV/POCV derate tables), and clock-tree insertion-delay estimate to justify the split.
signoff_risk: Too tight: fails STA, over-design. Too loose: silicon timing failure, chip doesn't meet frequency rating.
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: POCV adds significant uncertainty, typically 2-3x 28nm (confidence 0.6), requiring higher budget or statistical timing

pattern_name: Output delay budget to external device
situation: Chip outputs data to external device with known t_su and board trace delay; need set_output_delay to constrain internal logic.
derivation: Create virtual clock vclk with period T. set_output_delay -clock vclk -max T - t_su_ext - t_board_delay [get_ports OUT]. Assume T=10ns (confidence 0.2), t_su_ext=1ns (confidence 0.3), t_board=0.5ns (confidence 0.3). Output_delay = 10 - 1 - 0.5 = 8.5ns. Internal logic must produce data 8.5ns after clock edge. Slack = T - output_delay - T_internal_delay - T_skew.
wrong_way: Setting output_delay = 0 — internal logic gets full period but external device misses data because t_su not accounted. Silently breaks: STA passes, board-level system fails.
defense: Engineer presents external device t_su spec, board trace delay calculation, and system timing budget showing the subtraction arithmetic.
signoff_risk: Too tight: internal logic over-optimized, power/area wasted. Too loose: external device setup violation at system level, board failure.
